objectKey.description: claim check: an object-store key under the owner's prefix u/<owner_id>/ (never bytes)

seq.description: per-job sequence over every evt.run.* message of one run (= envelope job_id), starting at 1; the projector dedupes on (job_id, seq)

attempt.description: the run's attempt: 1, or 2 after the dispatcher lost the lease of attempt 1 and queued the run again (a run command is delivered once)

hostName.description: a GPU host's name: lower-case letters and digits (one NATS subject token)

envName.description: a runner env on a host (mlx, torch, native, fake)

workflowId.description: a registry workflow's slug (echo, qwen-image) or a user workflow's UUID (lower-case, which also fits this pattern)

nodeId.description: a node's id inside one workflow graph

nodeKind.description: a node schema's kind: a core node (prompt, output) or <family>/<node> (echo/echo)

portRef.description: <node id>.<output name> of another node in the same graph

scalarValue.description: an int, float, bool, string, text, enum or seed value; null only for a seed (random) or an image, media or span param left empty

imageRef.description: an Image value as a client writes it (RunRequest.inputs, batch rows, made_with, every pipelines message): a take of the caller, by id. Never an object key or a URL: studio resolves it (contracts/README.md, Image inputs)

image.description: an Image value as studio resolves it for cmd.run.execute: the take's immutable object, owned by the envelope's owner_id. The runner reads `key` from the object store and nothing else; its cache key for the image is (owner_id, key, etag). From API 1.14 the same form also carries a video take for a rows field of ref kind Media (an ask node's `media`): content_type video/mp4, its MP4 object, width and height of the video

key.description: the take's object, u/<owner_id>/runs/… or u/<owner_id>/uploads/…

etag.description: the object's ETag (quotes stripped) from studio's HEAD when it resolved the run; with the key, the content's identity for the runner's cache

loraId.description: a LoRA's id: a shared LoRA's is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of its file (the same file on two hosts is one LoRA); a user's own LoRA's is a UUID (contracts/README.md, LoRAs)

sha256.description: lower-case hex SHA-256 of a whole file

loraRef.description: a Lora value as a client writes it (a rows item's Lora field in RunRequest.inputs, workflows, presets, batch rows, made_with, every pipelines message): a LoRA the caller can use, by id. Never a path, key or URL: studio resolves it (contracts/README.md, LoRAs)

lora.description: a Lora value as studio resolves it for cmd.run.execute. shared: the runner finds the file by `sha256` in its own index (the dispatcher sent the run only to a host that lists it). own: the runner fetches `key` (under the envelope owner's u/<owner_id>/loras/) to its LoRA cache on first use and checks `bytes` and `sha256`

sha256.description: the file's content hash; = lora_id for a shared LoRA. The runner's cache identity for the LoRA

inputValue.description: a value in the client form (RunRequest.inputs, batch rows, made_with): a scalar, an Image as {take_id}, or a rows value (an ordered list of items, field → scalar, {take_id} or, for a Lora field, {lora_id}); from API 1.17 a frameRef in place of an Image (pipelines → studio.runs.create only); from API 1.19 a Media value as mediaRef and a span as spanValue; from API 1.22 a rows item's media field as mediaRef

resolvedValue.description: a value in cmd.run.execute: like inputValue, with every Image resolved to `image` and every Lora to `lora`; from API 1.19 every Media value resolved to `media` (from API 1.22 a rows item's media field too)

paramValue.description: a param value in a graph: inputValue (registry workflows, snapshots) or resolvedValue (cmd.run.execute). See registry.schema.json paramSchema for the types. From API 1.19 a `media` param: mediaRef (resolved: media); a `span` param: spanValue; from API 1.22 a rows item's media field: mediaRef (resolved: media)

params.description: param name → value; a param left out takes its node schema's default

in.description: input port name (or the name of a value param wired from upstream: contracts/README.md, Graph rules) → the output it is wired to

bypass.description: true = the node is switched off and passes its inputs through (contracts/README.md, Graph rules); absent = false. Never true in cmd.run.execute: studio splices bypassed nodes out before it sends a graph

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

only.description: API 1.19: enum param → the values this workflow allows (a subset of the schema's `enum`, holding the node's value): the form offers only those; another value is 422 `<node>.<param>: must be one of <values>`. LTX templates on the dev transformer pin `model.variant` to dev. Never in cmd.run.execute

optional.description: API 1.22: a core `image` node that may be left empty (its image null): studio then drops it and its wires before the run, so the optional inputs it feeds stay unwired (contracts/README.md, Graph rules: optional). Only on kind `image` whose wires all go to optional inputs (else the graph problem not_optional). Never in cmd.run.execute

graph.description: a workflow's node graph: node id → node

seed.description: a seed the runner actually used (exact in a JS number)

inputs.description: <node id>.<param name> → value (RunRequest.inputs); only the params to change

workflowSnapshot.description: a registry workflow or a user workflow as it was when the batch was submitted (a user workflow's nodes keep `bypass`, drop `position`; no `studio`); the batch runs this graph, never the live one

batchRow.description: a batch row number, from 1 (after seed repetition)

rowAttempt.description: a batch row's attempt: 1, +1 on every Retry of the row

idempotencyKey.description: <batch_id>:<row>:<row attempt>:<graph node>:<loop count>:<branch>, e.g. …:3:1:step:0:0. A batch of one workflow uses node `step`, loop 0, branch `0`. studio.runs.create returns the same run for the same key. A pipeline batch: <graph node> = the step node id, <loop count> = its visit in the row attempt from 0, <branch> = the seed index from 0. A judge, write or decide node of a pipeline batch (an LLM call): <graph node> = that node id, <loop count> = its visit from 0, <branch> = the call's run: 0, or 1 for the one re-ask after pipelines' own answer checks failed (contracts/README.md, Agent nodes). From API 1.15: a fanned-out step's run: <branch> = `<item index>-<seed index>` (both from 0); an Agent turn: <loop count> = the visit from 0, <branch> = `t<turn from 0>` (`t<turn>r` for its one re-ask); the director's chat: <row> = 0, <row attempt> = 1, <loop count> = the wake from 0, <branch> = `t<turn>` / `t<turn>r`

rowStatus.description: pipelines' view of a row: queued = not started; running = its run was requested and has not finished (a pipeline row: anywhere between its steps); waiting = parked on a gate for a pick (pipeline batches only)

batchStatus.description: set by pipelines_service (queued exists only in studio's record, before the first event)

takeIdList.description: at most 8 take ids (a step's seeds, a gate's candidates or pick)

pipelineSource.description: `$<input>`, `<step>.takes`, `<gate or judge>.picked`, from API 1.14 `<judge>.reasons` and `<memory read node>.notes` (text sources: write, decide and memory write `from` only) (contracts/README.md, Pipeline rules); from API 1.15 `<producer>.item` (in the binds of a step whose `each` is `<producer>.items`: this branch's item) and `<custom>.<output field>` (a custom node's output: a string field is a text source, a list of take ids a takes source). Which are allowed where: contracts/README.md, Pipeline rules; from API 1.17 `<step>.first_frame` / `<step>.last_frame` (a sequence's Re-render snapshot only): the first or last frame of that step's first take of its latest visit, sent to studio.runs.create as a frameRef

pipelineNode.description: a node of a pipeline snapshot: the document's node, a step's `inputs` already merged over its preset by studio at Submit, plus `seed_param`; from API 1.14 judge, write and decide nodes add `workflow` (the resolved ask workflow) and a judge's `criteria` is always both lists; from API 1.15 agent and custom nodes, a fanned-out step's `each` / `fanout_max`, a write's `list`, and every model node's `source`

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute
the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

preset.description: for display: already merged into inputs

inputs.description: the fixed values: the preset's, then the document's step inputs; from API 1.17 a sequence's Re-render snapshot may hold takes here (the clip's own images, checked at run as RunRequest.inputs)

bind.description: workflow param ← source; from API 1.17 a key `<node>.<param>[<row>]` (a sequence's Re-render snapshot only) fills the one Image field of that row (from 1) of the rows value in `inputs`, the row's other fields kept

looks.description: the step's look ids (PipelineStepNode.looks), for display: studio applies them from its batch copy when it makes the step's runs; pipelines ignores them

seed_param.description: the workflow's one unwired seed param that seeds vary; null without one

each.description: from API 1.15: fan out over this producer's list: one branch per item (Send), at most fanout_max

fanout_max.description: with each: the producer's list max

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute
the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute
the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

model.description: as in the document: auto, an ask workflow id, server:<name>[/<model>] or remote:<provider>/<model>

workflow.description: the ask workflow `model` resolved to at Submit (auto: contracts/README.md, Agent nodes: model); from API 1.15 `server-ask` for a local server, `remote` for a remote provider (no run)

memory.description: a memory read node: its examples (key = this judge's id) and notes go into the prompt

source.description: from API 1.15: where it runs (always sent from 1.15)

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

model.description: as in the document: auto, an ask workflow id, server:<name>[/<model>] or remote:<provider>/<model>

workflow.description: the ask workflow `model` resolved to at Submit (auto: contracts/README.md, Agent nodes: model); from API 1.15 `server-ask` for a local server, `remote` for a remote provider (no run)

source.description: from API 1.15: where it runs (always sent from 1.15)

oneOf.description: from API 1.15 a write with `list` has no `to`: it answers a list (its `<write>.items`)

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

model.description: as in the document: auto, an ask workflow id, server:<name>[/<model>] or remote:<provider>/<model>

workflow.description: the ask workflow `model` resolved to at Submit (auto: contracts/README.md, Agent nodes: model); from API 1.15 `server-ask` for a local server, `remote` for a remote provider (no run)

source.description: from API 1.15: where it runs (always sent from 1.15)

position.description: the node's place in the Graph view (canvas pixels, top-left of the card); absent = laid out by the client. Never in cmd.run.execute

oneOf.description: from API 1.15: an Agent (contracts/README.md, Agents), every default filled

routes.description: label → meaning; with a routes edge

wake_on_rows.description: director: which row ends wake its chat

oneOf.description: from API 1.15: a custom node (a pack's runnable in pipelines_service, contracts/README.md, Custom nodes)

version.description: the registered node's version at Submit

network.description: it calls the network: counted as a remote model

pipelineEdge.description: [from, to], [gate or judge, {pass, fail, max, then}] or (API 1.14) [decide, {routes: {label: to}, max, then: label}]

pipelineSnapshot.description: a saved pipeline as it was at Submit, with every workflow its steps use; the batch runs this, never the live documents

workflows.description: workflow id → its snapshot (as for a batch of one workflow)

providers.description: from API 1.15: every provider a node's source names, as it was at Submit

remote.description: from API 1.15 (always sent): the pipeline's remote switch and per-batch caps

status.description: a step: running (runs requested) then its end; a gate: waiting, picked, rejected; an output: succeeded; a judge: running (its call), then picked (a pass applied: Auto, or the user's pick), waiting (parked in Suggest), rejected (a fail verdict or the user rejected all) or failed (the call failed); write and decide: running, then succeeded or failed; memory: succeeded

run_ids.description: a step's runs, by seed index

take_ids.description: a step: its takes; a gate: the pick; an output: what it received

decision_id.description: judge, write, decide: the visit's decision

judged.description: a judge attempt's verdict summary (the run table's judged cell)

picked.description: takes kept (the user's pick once made)

suggested.description: the judge's pick (pre-selected in the review grid)

agreed.description: Suggest: the user's pick equalled the suggestion; null before a pick and in Auto

checks.description: every criterion's answer, musts then nices (additive in 1.14)

takes.description: every candidate with its reason, in candidate order (the attempts side by side)

route.description: a decide attempt: the route taken

branch.description: from API 1.15, a fanned-out step: one attempt per (visit, branch), branch = the item index

agent.description: from API 1.15, an agent attempt: the run table's cell (`4 turns · 6 tools · 14 shots`)

loop.description: a judge with a branch, a decide: its capped loop (retried <turns> of <max>; gave up → then)

turns.description: capped turns taken so far (a judge: its fail edge; a decide: its routes other than then)

criterion.description: one plain checklist line, e.g. `No extra or missing limbs`

judgeCriteria.description: a judge's checklist: every `must` passes for a take to pass; `nice` only orders the takes that pass. At most 12 lines in all, none twice (pipeline rule judge_criteria)

thumbKey.description: a derived thumbnail an ask run sent to the model: u/<owner_id>/llm/thumbs/<sha256 of the JPEG>.jpg, content-addressed, written once

seenItem.description: one thumbnail the model saw, in the order it saw them

frame.description: a video take's keyframe (frame index); null for an image take

error.description: why it did not pass (`answer did not match the schema: <validator error>`); null: it passed

tool_calls.description: from API 1.15, a server-ask run (or a remote call) with `tools`: the native OpenAI tool calls of the answer, as sent (pipelines normalises them into a turn)

arguments.description: the arguments as the model wrote them (JSON text)

answer.description: from API 1.14: the result of a run of a text (ask) workflow, stored on the run, never a take. The last try is the answer; a succeeded run's last try has error null and matches its `schema` (an empty schema: plain text). A failed run's tries are both failures (`answer did not match the schema: …`)

tries.description: 1, or 2 when the first did not parse or match the schema and the runner asked once more in the same run

seen.description: every thumbnail sent, in order (media items in order, a video's 3 keyframes in frame order)

tokens_in.description: prompt tokens, images included, over the tries

seconds.description: generation time over the tries (load not included)

decisionId.description: <batch_id>:<row>:<row attempt>:<node>:<visit from 1>: one judge, write or decide visit

replayKey.description: <batch_id>:<row>:<node>:<visit from 1>:<inputs hash> (contracts/README.md, Decisions: replay): a stored decision with this key is reused instead of asking the model

modelRef.description: the ask workflow's <family>/model node as it ran (made_with.model's shape)

decision.description: from API 1.14: what one judge, write or decide visit decided and from what (plan 16.7). Made by pipelines, published in evt.pipeline.step, stored by studio on the batch row and on the takes it affected (a judge: its candidates). `judge`, `write` or `decide` holds the derived result for its kind; absent when `error` is set before one was derived

replayed.description: true: taken from a stored decision with the same replay key (Resume, Retry, Run again with the same decisions); no model was asked

replayed_from.description: with replayed: the decision it reused

run_ids.description: the ask runs (branch 0, and 1 after pipelines' own checks failed); empty when replayed; an agent: one per turn (and re-ask)

workflow.description: the ask workflow that answered (resolved at Submit)

template.description: the prompt template and its version

prompt.description: the filled prompt of the last run

seen.description: the thumbnails the model saw on this visit; [] for a replayed decision (its replayed_from holds them)

answers.description: every try of every run, in order; the last one with error null is what was decided

memory_read.description: the memory items (from the batch's snapshot) the prompt used

error.description: the call failed (its run failed, or both answers failed the checks): the row failed with it

checks.description: one per criterion, must lines then nice lines, true = passes

rank.description: its place in the derived order (1 = best)

picked.description: the first keep takes of the derived order that pass, when verdict is pass; [] when fail

verdict.description: pass: at least keep takes pass

first_failed.description: the best take's first must that is false; null when it passes

forced.description: the loop cap forced the `then` route; the model's route was not followed

source.description: from API 1.15: where the model ran (absent = local)

replayable.description: from API 1.15: false for a remote decision (never reused: Run again with the same decisions asks it again)

network_failures.description: from API 1.15, remote: transport failures retried during the visit (never verdicts)

agent.description: from API 1.15, an agent visit: its turns (the execution view's messages and tool calls) and what it ended with

stopped.description: null: it finished; else the cap that ended it (an item failure)

kind.description: pick: a pick with a note at a judge; node: a memory write node; user: typed in the Memory panel

memoryItem.description: from API 1.14: one item of a pipeline's memory (namespace <owner_id>/pipeline/<pipeline_id>, LangGraph's store in pipelines). Never images: takes by id

key.description: a note's key (a memory write node's, or the user's; null = none); a judge example's: its judge node id

text.description: a note's text; an example's note (the user's words at the pick)

kept.description: an example: the takes the user picked ([] when they rejected all)

rejected.description: an example: the candidates not picked

agreed.description: an example: the pick equalled the judge's suggestion; null for a note

memorySnapshot.description: the copy of the pipeline's memory a batch reads (taken when pipelines starts the batch); every read of the batch uses it

modelSource.description: from API 1.15: where a judge, write, decide or agent node's model runs, resolved at Submit (contracts/README.md, Model sources). local: an ask workflow run by a runner; server: a local server you run (its calls are runs of the built-in `server-ask` workflow, released by the dispatcher on `host`); remote: a provider outside the machine (calls made by pipelines_service, never a run, never replayed)

providerName.description: a model provider's name (a local server or a remote provider), set by the admin

providerModel.description: a model name as the provider's OpenAI-compatible API takes it (`qwen2.5vl:7b`, `gpt-4.1-mini`)

providerSnapshot.description: from API 1.15: a provider as it was at Submit (pipelines calls it from this, never from the live settings). base_url is configuration, not a media link (the claim-check rule is about object keys). key_secret names a file in pipelines_service's secrets directory; the key itself never travels

host.description: server: the GPU host whose memory it shares

memory_gb.description: server: the memory reserved for it on host

key_secret.description: remote: the secret file's name; server: null (no key)

max_in_flight.description: remote: calls in flight at once over every batch (default 2)

remoteSettings.description: from API 1.15: the pipeline's switch for calls that leave the machine, filled by studio (off when the document has none). The caps are per batch, over every row and the director's chat

agentCaps.description: from API 1.15: an Agent's hard caps per visit (the director's chat: per wake)

max_tokens.description: prompt + answer tokens over the visit's turns, as the model reported them

listSpec.description: from API 1.15: the node answers a list of texts (a shot list), 1 to max items: `<node>.items`, which a step fans out over (`each`)

frameRef.description: from API 1.17, only in a studio.runs.create request of a sequence's Re-render (a bound `<step>.first_frame` / `<step>.last_frame` source): the first or last frame of that video take. Studio resolves it to the frame take (POST /v1/studio/takes/{take_id}/frame, made at once from the stored poster or last frame) and the run records `{take_id}` of the frame take; a take without a stored last frame fails the run's row (`… take <id> has no stored last frame`)

videoStream.description: from API 1.17: the video stream's facts as ffprobe reads them from the written file (what the export plan compares: contracts/README.md, Timeline: export plan). A runner that writes the MP4 itself (the fake) reports what it wrote

container.description: the first name of ffprobe's format_name (mov,mp4,… → mp4 for .mp4, mov for .mov)

sar.description: sample aspect ratio; null when unset

field_order.description: progressive, tt, bb, …; null when unknown

color.description: the four colour tags; null = untagged (an untagged value is still compared)

extradata_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the codec header data (SPS/PPS): ffprobe -show_data_hash sha256

mediaRef.description: a Media value as a client writes it (API 1.19; a `media` param, contracts/README.md, Media inputs): a video or audio take of the caller by id. `in` / `out` (seconds of the take's own time, studio snaps them: a video's frames, audio to the millisecond) only on a param with `trim`: the part it reads (absent: 0 / the take's end). Never an object key or a URL

spanValue.description: a `span` param's value (API 1.19): a time range on the workflow's one video source, in that take's own seconds; start < end, end at most the take's duration (contracts/README.md, Media inputs)

media.description: a Media value as studio resolves it for cmd.run.execute (API 1.19): the take's immutable object under the envelope owner's prefix and the facts studio checked. The runner reads `key` only; its cache key is (owner_id, key, etag) plus in/out. A video take in an audio input: its MP4, read for its sound

in.description: a `trim` param or rows item field (API 1.22) only, always present there: the snapped start (default 0)

out.description: a `trim` param or rows item field (API 1.22) only, always present there: the snapped end (default min(duration_s, max_s))

sourceMap.description: API 1.19: how an output's time lines up with the media take it was made from (retake, extend, audio to video): output time t = source time t + offset_s; the part the model generated is [new_in_s, new_out_s) of the output. The Timeline's fill uses it (contracts/README.md, Timeline: take actions)
